answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash of deposited funds. Like a rare marble shard in a mosaic, each unit anchors an identity. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times that expense. A violet signal denotes audit success, treating each byte as a relic of provenance that survives the 30-day binding period to ensure integrity.
